phaseA.method: each identity mapped by bracketing: pitBlock is monotone in pc within the method (verified True for both methods), and each method has in-method calibration points from the committed G5b/G5c manifests (pc, pitBlock, pitIndex). The target's pitBlock therefore brackets a byte window containing exactly one candidate instruction of the mutated kind.
phaseA.pitCounterNote: PIT never reports bytecode offsets, and its block/index counter counts ASM nodes that javap does not expose (a label/line-count reconstruction matched only 4/36 calibration identities). Bracketing is therefore used, and it is validated by in-method monotonicity plus the uniqueness of each candidate window.

proof: Each mutated instruction lies on the suspension protocol of one specific call: resolveGovernedSuspension() at source line 145 in suspendToolExecution, and resolveGovernedIdentity(workflowRunId) at source line 82 in requestApproval.

Both callees are declared suspend, but neither body contains a suspension point: resolveGovernedSuspension has 50 instructions with 0 getCOROUTINE_SUSPENDED loads and 0 if_acmpne; resolveGovernedIdentity-jFE5hGw has 32 instructions with 0 getCOROUTINE_SUSPENDED and 0 if_acmpne, invoking only Continuation.getContext, GovernedRunScope$Key accessors, GovernedRunIdentity/RunId getters, Intrinsics.areEqual, makeConcatWithConstants and an exception constructor.
GovernedRunScope.resolve(context) is an ordinary non-suspend function; currentCoroutineContext()/Continuation.getContext do not suspend.

A suspend function can return COROUTINE_SUSPENDED only through the sentinel comparison emitted after a call. With no such comparison and no suspending callee, both resolvers always return their value directly.

Therefore in each caller the sentinel test is always false, so the COROUTINE_SUSPENDED exit (pc163, pc164) cannot execute; and the resumed continuation for that call can only be constructed by a real suspension at that call, so the resumed-path throwOnFailure (pc194, pc204) cannot execute.
Nothing else branches to those instructions: no branch or switch entry in either method targets pc194 or pc204.
phaseC.whyNotToolingLimitation: No independent evidence shows the instruction executing while PIT fails to attribute coverage. The instructions cannot execute at all.
phaseC.whyNotEquivalent: Equivalence answers a different question. These mutants never cross the reachability boundary, so equivalence is neither claimed nor needed.
phaseC.whyNoTestAdded: Tests are required only for identities proven REACHABLE. A test cannot make an unreachable instruction execute without either changing production semantics or fabricating a coroutine state, both forbidden. Adding one would be 'making PIT green' rather than explaining behaviour.
